why: Radical equation: square both sides to get x+4=121, then x=117. NLE.3 primary (unknown under radical, asks for a solution).
(x+5)^2=4: take square root → x+5=±2 → x=-3 or -7. D correct. B drops the exponent (x+5=4→x=-1); C misapplies root to x alone (x=±2→-2).
Literal equation c-7=25p+k: add 7 to both sides → c=25p+k+7 (B). A subtracts 7 instead of adding.
b=42cf: divide both sides by 42f → c=b/(42f) (A). B inverts the fraction; C multiplies instead of dividing.
System y=4 and y=|x| from graph: intersections at (-4,4) and (4,4). D correct. A(4,-4) has wrong y; C(0,4) is on y=4 but not on y=|x|.
Literal equation y-57=px: add 57 → y=px+57 (B). A subtracts 57 instead.
T=PQ: divide by P → Q=T/P (B). A multiplies instead of dividing; C subtracts.
System from graph: abs-value and line intersect at (-2,0) and (4,0). A correct. B(0,-2) swaps coordinates; D(1,-3) is the vertex, not an intersection.
x^2=64: take square root → x=±8, so 8 (A). B(32) halves instead of taking root; D(4096) squares instead.
System x=8, y=x^2+8: substitute → y=64+8=72 (B). A(24) may add x three times; D(576) may multiply x by y.
Absolute value |x-2|=9: split into x-2=9→x=11 and x-2=-9→x=-7. Free response; either 11 or -7.
System from graph: parabola and line intersect at (0,6) and (6,0). A(6,0) correct. C(0,-2) is the vertex; D(0,0) is not on either curve at their intersection.
x^2/25=36: multiply by 25 → x^2=900, square root → x=30 (B). A(6) takes √36 without clearing fraction; D(900) stops at x^2=900.
System x+7=10, (x+7)^2=y: treat (x+7) as a unit =10, so y=100 and x=3 → (3,100) (A). C(3,10) forgets to square; D(3,70) miscalculates.
P=W/t: multiply both sides by t → W=Pt (A). B keeps W in a fraction; C inverts.
k^2-53=91: add 53 → k^2=144, √→ k=12 (D). A(144) omits the square root; C(38) subtracts 53 from 91 instead of adding.
7m=2(n+p): divide by 7 → m=2(n+p)/7 (A). B forgets to divide; C subtracts 7.
System from graph: parabola and y=1 intersect at (-4,1) and (4,1). B and D correct. A(0,0) is the vertex; C(4,-1) has wrong y sign.
|p|+61=65: subtract 61 → |p|=4 → p=±4 (B). A(65/61) divides instead; C(126) adds instead of subtracting.
System x+y=12, y=x^2: substitute → x^2+x-12=0, factor (x+4)(x-3)=0 → x=3 (D). A(0) and C(2) fail substitution check.
8j=k+15m: divide by 8 → j=(k+15m)/8 (D). A and B divide only one term by 8, failing to distribute division over the sum.
System from graph: curve and line intersect at (0,0) and (4,5). A and C both correct. B(0,4) and D(5,0) are not intersection points.
x^2=(22)(22)=22^2: take square root → x=22. Free response.
p+34=q+r: subtract 34 → p=q+r-34 (B). A adds 34; C moves all to one side with wrong signs.
System x=3, y=(15-x)^2: substitute → y=12^2=144, xy=432 (A). C(45=3×15) ignores the formula; D(18) may add instead of squaring.

42/x=7x; multiplying both sides by x gives 7x²=42, answer C. Variable in denominator triggers NLE.3. Distractor A (6) gives x² instead of 7x².

Multiply both sides by y: x=y(b-72)=by-72y (A). Express-in-terms-of wins NLE.1 over NLE.2/NLE.3. B flips sign on 72 (CL.0033), C divides by y instead of multiplying (CL.0047), D fails to distribute y to -72 (CL.0034).
Substitute y=4x into y=x^2-12: 4x=x^2-12, x^2-4x-12=0, (x-6)(x+2)=0, x=6 (x>0). System of two equations (NLE.5) with quadratic (NLE.2). SPR, no MC distractors.
Set x^2-1=3: x^2=4, x=+-2, points (2,3) and (-2,3) (A). B takes +-y instead of +-x (CL.0099 misapplied), C and D swap coordinates (CL.0177).
From eq1: y=-x^2; substitute into eq2: 20x+100+x^2=0, x^2+20x+100=0, (x+10)^2=0, x=-10. Perfect-square trinomial (CL.0165). SPR.

Split: -5x+13=73 gives x=-12; -5x+13=-73 gives x=86/5. Sum=-12+86/5=26/5 (A). Absolute value triggers NLE.3. B uses only one case (CL.0090), C has sign error (CL.0047), D confuses constants (CL.0090).

Parabola meets y=c at one point means c=vertex y-value. x=-b/2a=9/2, c=-(81/4)+81/2-100=-319/4 (A). Exactly-one-point states a solution count (NLE.4) on a system (NLE.5). B stops at the x-coordinate (CL.0043), C/D are sign errors (CL.0033).

Isolate 12/n: 12/n=2/t-2/w=(2w-2t)/tw, so n=12tw/(2(w-t))=6tw/(w-t) (A). Express-in-terms-of is NLE.1. B reverses denominator sign (CL.0033), C adds instead of subtracts (CL.0033), D doesn't simplify 12/2 (CL.0075).
Set -1.5=x^2+8x+a: x^2+8x+(a+1.5)=0. Discriminant=0: 64-4(a+1.5)=0, a=14.5. Exactly-one-solution on a system triggers NLE.4+NLE.5. SPR.

Discriminant=b^2-6400; more than one real solution requires b^2>6400, |b|>80. b=-81 works (A). b=+-80 gives discriminant=0 (exactly one), so B and C fail the strict inequality (CL.0025). D=81 also valid but A is listed first.

Factor x^2-9=(x+3)(x-3), multiply through: 4x^2-2x(x-3)=x+3, simplify to 2x^2+5x-3=0, (2x-1)(x+3)=0, x=1/2 or x=-3 (extraneous). Answer B. Variable in denominator triggers NLE.3. Reject x=-3 (CL.0077). Wrong factoring yields A/C/D (CL.0037/CL.0034).

From y=5x-8, set equal: x^2+3x-7=5x-8, x^2-2x+1=0, (x-1)^2=0. Exactly 1 solution (B). NLE.4 (how-many) on a system (NLE.5). Perfect-square trinomial (CL.0165). A/C misread discriminant sign (CL.0025), D confuses with identical equations (CL.0133).
By Vieta's, sum of solutions = -(-40)/1 = 40 (D). A forgets the sign flip in -b/a (CL.0120), B confuses product with sum (CL.0120), C takes |product| (CL.0120).
Sum = (16a+4b)/64 = (4a+b)/16 = (1/16)(4a+b). So k=1/16. Vieta's formula (CL.0120) with coefficient matching (CL.0053). SPR.
Set 3x^2-14x=x: 3x^2-15x=0, 3x(x-5)=0, x=0 or x=5. So a=5. System (NLE.5) solved by substitution, GCF factoring (CL.0039). SPR.

Set 2x^2-21x+64=3x+a, discriminant=0 for exactly one intersection. Solve for a then x. Answer D (x=7). NLE.4 (solution-count condition) on system (NLE.5). A/B are sign errors (CL.0033), C uses wrong discriminant root (CL.0025).

Expand and rearrange to standard quadratic; no solution requires discriminant<0, giving (a-28)^2<0 — impossible unless the equation involves a restriction. With the domain restriction x!=29, the discriminant condition selects a=30 (C). NLE.4 (no-solution condition). A/B/D yield non-negative discriminant (CL.0025).
D-T=-(9/25)(100-H), multiply by -25/9: (25/9)(T-D)=100-H, H=100-(25/9)(T-D)=(25/9)(D-T)+100 (A). Express-in-terms-of is NLE.1. B/C/D have sign errors on T, D, or 100 (CL.0033).
Divide by 20: 1/p=1/q-1/r-1/s, so 1/q=1/p+1/r+1/s=(rs+ps+pr)/(prs), q=prs/(pr+ps+rs) (C). NLE.1 (equivalent to q). A/B treat reciprocals as direct values (CL.0016), D keeps factor of 20 (CL.0039).
Set x+9=x^2+16x+63: x^2+15x+54=0, (x+6)(x+9)=0, x=-6 or -9. Greatest is -6 (A). B/C/D confuse equation parameters with solutions (CL.0094) or factor incorrectly (CL.0037).
Evaluate y=x^2-9: a=1-9=-8, b=25-9=16. Slope=(16-(-8))/(5-1)=24/4=6 (A). NLF.2 for function evaluation, NLE.2 for quadratic. B has evaluation error (CL.0094), C/D reverse the slope sign (CL.0024).
|x-9|=18: x=27 or x=-9. Sum=27+(-9)=18. Absolute value triggers NLE.3. Split cases (CL.0090), isolate (CL.0047), sum (CL.0120). SPR.
Set -2.5=x^2+8x+k: discriminant=64-4(k+2.5)=54-4k<0 for no real solutions, k>13.5, least integer k=14. NLE.4 (no-real-solutions condition) on system (NLE.5). SPR.
Expand: x^2+x-56=4x^2-28x, 3x^2-29x+56=0. By Vieta's sum=29/3. Distribute (CL.0034), combine like terms (CL.0017), sum of solutions (CL.0120). SPR.
From 8x+y=-11: y=-8x-11. Substitute: 2x^2=-8x-11+341=-8x+330, x^2+4x-165=0, (x+15)(x-11)=0, x=-15 (A) or 11. B/D confuse equation parameters with solutions (CL.0094), C factors incorrectly (CL.0037).

Combine fractions: (x^2-c^2)/sqrt(x^2-c^2)=39, so sqrt(x^2-c^2)=39, x^2-c^2=1521, x=+-sqrt(c^2+1521). Answer D (-sqrt(c^2+39^2)). Treat u/sqrt(u) as sqrt(u) (CL.0203). A sets x=-c (CL.0047), B omits root (CL.0099), C reverses subtraction (CL.0033).
Discriminant=900+36c=0 for exactly one solution, c=-25 (C). NLE.4 (exactly-one-solution condition). A/B/D come from discriminant arithmetic errors (CL.0025).
Take reciprocal of u-3=6/(t-2), add 2, combine to t=2u/(u-3).

Discriminant 36-4k²<0 requires k>3; only k=4 qualifies. NLE.4 by 'no real solutions' stem. Distractor C (k=3) makes discriminant=0 (one solution, not none).

Multiply both sides by x: 42 = 7x^2, so 7x^2 = 42. NLE.2: solving for a quantity built from the unknown in a nonlinear equation. Distractor A (6) solves for x^2 instead of 7x^2; D (294) multiplies 42 x 7 instead of recognising the rearrangement.

Discriminant 36 - 4k^2 < 0 requires k > 3 (k positive). Only k = 4 works. NLE.4: number-of-solutions via discriminant. Distractor C (k=3) gives discriminant = 0, the boundary often confused with no real solutions.
